A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BEVLM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across pagination changes and moves between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation comparisons, open-loop and closed-loop driving experiments, ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds alternative-supervision comparisons and evaluation using VAD.

M1.justification: The BEV tokenization, MLP projector, frozen LLM teacher, VQA supervision, and joint detection regularization remain unchanged. Coordinate conversion moves from Appendix A.4 into Section 4.1. Applying the same distilled encoder to VAD extends evaluation without changing the proposed distillation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use DriveLM-nuScenes, Ego3D, nuScenes planning evaluation, and NeuroNCAP safety-critical scenarios. VAD and the new supervision controls operate within this retained coverage. The five qualitative driving cases are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds a randomly initialized auxiliary VQA head and two implemented VLM-AD-style comparators, labeled VLM-AD trans. and VLM-AD CLIP. These substantially expand the planning comparison beyond the undistilled baseline. Section 5.4 distinguishes these implementations from unavailable original VLM-AD resources.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include training VAD decoder heads for 12 epochs with the transferred encoder frozen and matching the auxiliary control's approximately 13M trainable parameters to the projector. VLM-AD-style controls use automatically labeled answers. Existing dataset splits, metrics, and the 20-epoch UniAD training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 directly tests whether pretrained LLM semantics provide benefits beyond an auxiliary VQA objective and compares alternative semantic-supervision designs. The VAD experiment additionally tests transfer across driving pipelines. These substantially strengthen the diagnostic evidence; existing downsampling, VQA-subset, and qualitative failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports NeuroNCAP scores and collision rates as mean ± standard deviation over 50 random-seed runs, including Tables 4 and 6. v1 provides point estimates without corresponding run-count or uncertainty information. This substantially changes statistical reporting but does not establish that the run count increased.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces UniAD baseline/1B/8B NeuroNCAP scores of 2.10/2.46/2.71 with 2.38/2.93/3.05, revises collision rates, and adds VAD and alternative-supervision results. Table 6 revises impact velocities and subset rankings. Smaller corrections include Table 2 accuracy from 95.2 to 95.3 and the stated Ego3D L1 reduction from 27.8% to 21.8%. With newly documented 50-seed reporting, the closed-loop revisions should not be interpreted as established same-protocol performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The latent-alignment relation in Equation 1 and the next-token training objective in Appendix A.4 remain unchanged. The semantic-manifold explanation is condensed, without changing formal mathematical reasoning or introducing or removing proofs.

C1.justification: The central representation and semantic-distillation contributions remain intact. The abstract and introduction now explicitly claim benefits across UniAD and VAD. The headline safety-score improvement changes from 29.0% to 28.2%, and the introduction's collision-rate reduction changes from 11.3% to 16.1%.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 adds explanations attributing the controls' weaker performance to missing pretrained semantics, weaker CLIP-space supervision, and less direct integration with the LLM. The VQA-ablation interpretation changes from Behavior/Planning dominance to comparable, complementary subsets; the combined subset no longer has the lowest reported impact velocity.

D1.justification: v2 documents the VAD training schedule, parameter matching for the auxiliary control, and answer generation and supervision details for the VLM-AD-style variants. It adds a project website but removes Appendix F's resource URLs and license inventory. Most existing hyperparameters, hardware information, and implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: VLM-AD, already cited in v1, receives a substantive methodological comparison in new Section 5.4. References to SpatialVLM and the original Vision Transformer paper are removed. Updates to DrivingGPT and Orion publication metadata do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introductory and semantic-manifold explanations, moves coordinate conversion into the main method section, inserts Section 5.4, updates acknowledgments, and removes the resource appendix. These are localized edits and organizational adjustments within a largely retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains pipeline grouping and additional comparison rows, while Table 6 reorders metrics and accommodates uncertainty reporting. Table highlighting and spacing change. Existing figures are retained and relocated or renumbered, including the velocity plot moving from Figure D.1 to Figure 8; no new qualitative figure content is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central distillation claim through controls for alternative explanations, transfer to VAD, and explicit simulation uncertainty reporting (Sections 5.1–5.4 and Tables 4–6). These address important weaknesses in v1's planning evidence rather than merely increasing reported performance. VAD still shares the BEV encoder architecture, limiting the generality established. Removing the resource-access appendix is a modest reproducibility loss, outweighed by the stronger experimental evidence and transparency.
